data.title: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI rout deepens
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asia stocks on track for worst week since Covid hit
  • Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade
  • Dollar holds near 19-month peak on safe-haven flows

By Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

Asian shares tumbled on Friday, heading for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in the AI sector, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) lost 3.3%, its biggest single-day drop in nearly four months. The gauge has now sunk 8.5% this week, its worst performance since March 2020, when COVID was sweeping the globe.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 5% and registered a 7.7% weekly drop, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 5.2% and ended the week 8% lower. Taiwan shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 6.2% on Friday and 17.5% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990.

The moves in Asia followed losses of more than 2% for the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and the Nasdaq Composite on Thursday after Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, saw its shares surge in a historic debut but the euphoria failed to lift other stocks.

"Risk aversion intensified as investors continued to unwind crowded positioning and reassess the broader macro backdrop following Anthropic's record-shattering IPO," said Preston Pagli, markets analyst at Citi.

Nvidia's blowout earnings earlier in the week were not the reset markets had hoped for, while sentiment deteriorated further after Anthropic's IPO failed to spark a broader rally, he added.

Adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

All of that has piled further pressure on the AI trade, already battered in recent weeks by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, growing momentum for the anti-data-centre movement following Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections, and concerns over the sector's rising debt loads.

"No one headline drove the roll, though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment. Overall, it just felt like more questions than answers out there today with most wondering what gets this tape to feel better?" said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

They said asset managers and hedge funds net-sold macro products while they net-bought pockets of consumer and financials, with liquidity remaining poor, which is exacerbating price action.

The painful selloff now looks set to spill beyond Asia, with pan-European Euro Stoxx 50 futures down 1.7% at 6,017. US stock futures also pointed to further losses, with the S&P 500 futures down 0.5% and Nasdaq futures down 1% in Asia.

DOLLAR EXTENDS RALLY, TREASURY YIELDS DIP ON RISK AVERSION

As risk sentiment took a beating, the US dollar extended its rally on safe-haven bids, while also being supported by growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

The dollar index last traded steady at 103.86, after rising to its highest since April 2025 this week, and is now on track to post its fourth week of gains.

In government debt, US Treasury yields eased as the sharp equity retreat drove investors into safe-haven bonds. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes fell for a fifth straight session, to 5%, while the two-year yield (US2YT=RR) touched a 10-day low of 4.7216%.

Oil prices were mostly steady, with Brent crude futures up 0.4% to $92.37 a barrel but on track for a third week of declines. Reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus. (O/R)

Non-interest-bearing gold slid 2% to $3,552.20 an ounce and was headed for a 8.5% weekly loss.

data.title: Rupee rises past 93/USD as AI rout draws billions into India, speculators bail
data.description:
Key points:
  • Rupee trims 2026 losses to 3.5% from nearly 8% in May
  • Bankers say hedge funds unwound bearish rupee wagers this week
  • Overseas investors pour more than $12 billion into Indian stocks in November

By Jaspreet Kalra

The Indian rupee strengthened past the psychologically important 93-per-dollar mark on Friday for the first time since April, as a rebound in capital inflows and easing oil prices accelerated a rapid reversal in the currency's fortunes.

The unit has struggled for most of 2026 and threatened to breach record low levels as recently as last month. It has since recovered sharply, cutting its year-to-date losses to 3.5% compared to nearly 8% at its weakest point in May.

Friday's gains came as the global rout in AI stocks worsened, although Indian equities held steady. The benchmark Nifty 50 was up 0.1%, while MSCI's gauge of Asian stocks (..MIAP00000PUS) slid 3.5%.

Overseas investors have poured more than $12 billion into Indian stocks so far in November, according to depository data, drawn by the market's relatively limited exposure to the AI theme.

"The rupee rallying past 93 is directly a function of increased portfolio inflows, offshore bearish bets unwinding and policy influence," said Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and economist at ANZ.

"Importantly, the RBI is choosing to let the INR appreciate and not draw a floor by buying reserves to elicit a behavioural or expectation shift among exporters and offshore participants."

The surge of inflows has increased the supply of dollars in the market and boosted the rupee at a time when the Reserve Bank of India's measures have curbed demand.

Earlier this year, policymakers rolled out measures to support the unit as it came under sustained pressure, including clamping down on speculative trades, attracting capital inflows from overseas Indians and slowing down dollar demand in the market.

As the rupee struggled near record low levels of 97 last month, RBI chief Sanjay Malhotra had hinted that monetary tightening could be used to support the unit.

A sustained recovery may help reverse capital outflow-induced weakness in the currency, which has eroded returns for foreign investors and could deter further investments.

OFFSHORE RUPEE BEARS BAIL

The rupee has also benefitted from a rush to unwind bearish wagers on the currency this week.

The reversal, which four bankers said was led by overseas hedge funds, has been aggressive enough to lift the rupee to a premium in the non-deliverable forward market compared to onshore forwards.

The 1-month USD/INR NDF was last at 93.26 compared to 93.43 for the 1-month onshore forward.

"The shift appears material and somewhat sticky. A combination of better global dynamics, high negative carry, and clean positioning has capitulated the rupee to outperform dramatically," Bofa Global Research said in a note.

Options markets have reflected the change in sentiment, with a key gauge showing that demand for options betting on rupee weakness has eased relative to those betting on its strength.

data.title: Webuild Now Holds Over 60% Stake in Trevi
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Italian construction and civil engineering company Webuild said late Thursday that it now holds 60.82% of the shares in Trevi-Finanziaria Industriale through share purchases and offer acceptances.

Webuild earlier this week received clearance for the takeover from the Italian Competition Authority. The regulator decided not to open an inquiry as it doesn't significantly impede effective competition in the markets concerned and doesn't entail the creation or strengthening of a dominant position, Webuild said.

Webuild made an initial bid of 4.50 euros per share for Trevi in July, before later agreeing to pay 5.165 euros a share, or around 339 million euros ($371.8 million).

In a statement Thursday, Webuild Chief Executive Pietro Salini said that the deal has now effectively come to fruition and "allows the group to unlock significant synergies, strengthening the competitiveness of the entire supply chain across Italy's industrial system."

The offer, which is mandatory and not subject to any conditions, closes Friday.

data.title: Anthropic's Australian data centre overwhelmingly opposed by residents
data.description:
Key points:
  • Project draws 595 objections or delay requests from nearly 600 public submissions, filing shows
  • Data centre's planned computing load reaches 1.44 gigawatts, among Australia's biggest
  • Most objections cite water, power, noise, road damage and housing concerns

By Byron Kaye

A data centre planned in regional Australia with Anthropic as its anchor tenant is overwhelmingly opposed by residents, a filing for the project showed, setting the scene for a showdown between the AI company and the community hosting its first Australian facility.

Of nearly 600 public submissions on the proposed Western Downs Digital Park, about 250 km (155 miles) west of Brisbane, two expressed support for the project and one was neutral, according to the filing. The remaining 595 opposed it or asked for a delay until developers cleared certain environmental hurdles, the filing said.

"A significant number of submissions raise reasonable matters regarding water, power, noise, roads, housing and the scale of the project," the filing, lodged on behalf of developer Zerra DC, said.

A Zerra spokesperson said the project took seriously the submissions, which "reinforce that people want a greater say in how the project develops". The developer was expanding its community engagement and planned to report changes demanded by the public.

Anthropic declined to comment.

The initial response, though far from binding, gives a sense of the souring relationship between communities and the so-called AI factories being built at pace around the world in a boom McKinsey has valued at $7 trillion by 2030.

Already in Australia, Goodman Group scrapped a roughly A$1.2 billion data centre planned for Sydney in September after a public backlash, while NextDC delayed a project in Melbourne amid resident concerns about energy use, triggering a shares selldown.

The Anthropic project is on farmland and further from the suburbs, but with a planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would be one of the country's biggest. About one-third of the submissions were from people who lived within 200 km of the site, the filing said.

Objectors mostly cited concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction traffic and pressure on housing.

Before the data centre project named Anthropic as its tenant on September 15, it had received five objections in a month, a log of public comments showed, with the rest arriving between then and November 11, when the local government stopped accepting submissions.

The filing about Australian data centre submissions was published the same week Anthropic made its stock market debut on Wall St, pricing its initial public offering on November 18 in a deal that valued the company at around $1.5 trillion.

data.title: Turkey's Kiler Holding rejects lawmaker's share transaction allegations, files criminal complaint
data.description:
Kiler Holding , a Turkish conglomerate, has rejected a lawmaker's allegations concerning share transactions involving the company and its shareholders, saying it had filed a criminal complaint against him and lawsuits seeking damages.

Umit Ozlale, a member of the opposition New Party, questioned a series of share sales, purchases and transfers involving Kiler shareholders and a fund in comments at a press conference in parliament and in a post on X. He also asked whether Turkey's Capital Markets Board, or SPK, had reviewed the transactions.

Ozlale has been a leading figure among those in parliament trying to scrutinise Turkey’s recent investment funds crisis.

Kiler Holding, which is active in sectors including construction and energy, said in a statement on Thursday evening that the allegations were unfounded and that the company and its shareholders were being targeted for political reasons.

The company said all the transactions complied with relevant regulations and that the required disclosures had been made through the public disclosure platform KAP.

Records relating to the transactions were transparent and available for independent audit and examination by the relevant authorities, it said.

data.title: SpaceX sells $32B in AI chip debt above 8% yield: report
data.description:
Key points:
  • SpaceX sold $32B of bonds to fund its purchase of artificial intelligence chips on Thursday, in a complicated and relatively high-yielding transaction that may serve as a model for a wave of similar financings to come, according to a Bloomberg report.
  • The debt offering was designed to keep the borrowing off SpaceX’s balance sheet and is part of a more than $40B financing that also includes bank loans.
  • The deal will effectively allow SpaceX to buy Nvidia Corp. chips that the rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company will lease for about five years.
  • The debt was sold on Thursday in three parts, the report said. Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Apollo Global Management Inc ran the transaction.
  • The biggest of the three portions sold on Thursday, about $25.2B of Class A3 notes, was priced at a yield of 8.259%, a relatively high level for an investment-grade security. The average US high-grade note yielded 5.95% on Thursday, according to Bloomberg index data. The bonds also offered a premium over SpaceX’s existing debt from its June offering, which tanked in the secondary market after the securities started trading.
